stories.headline: IMD update: Third cyclone on trot developing over Bay by Monday
stories.title: IMD update: Third cyclone on trot developing over Bay by Monday
stories.summary: If the forecasts hold, this would be the third cyclone over the Bay of Bengal in quick succession during ongoing North-East monsoon season after severe cyclones Arnab and Murasu late last month
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Bay of Bengal is once again emerging as a potential breeding ground for a cyclone, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) flagging a fresh formation alert over its central parts by Monday evening.

A low-pressure area that lay over the south-east Bay on Friday is forecast to intensify into a depression by Sunday before rapidly strengthening in two successive stages over exceptionally warm ocean waters.
If the forecasts hold, this would be the third cyclone in quick succession during the ongoing North-East monsoon season.

Severe cyclones Arnab and Murasu had struck the Andhra Pradesh coast in rapid succession late last month, even as a developing El Niño over the equatorial eastern Pacific presented a seemingly contradictory backdrop to the unusually active storm season.

With the Bay continuing to host an active MJO pulse and oceanic conditions remaining favourable, the coming days will be crucial in determining whether the developing ‘low’ graduates into another powerful cyclone.
The immediate focus will be on how quickly it organises, how long it retains access to favourable atmospheric conditions, and, eventually, which stretch of the eastern seaboard it threatens.

The emerging system is drawing support from an active Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO), which has gained considerable amplitude over the Bay before preparing to resume its eastward journey towards the South China Sea.
The MJO is an eastward-moving pulse of enhanced cloud formation, thunderstorms and atmospheric circulation along the tropics.

When its active phase passes over a tropical ocean basin, it can create conditions conducive to cyclone formation by encouraging rising air, strengthening low-level atmospheric rotation and reducing the disruptive influence of vertical wind shear, or changes in wind speed and direction with height.
The MJO is therefore favouring cyclogenesis over both the Bay and the Arabian Sea, although this does not necessarily imply that El Niño is contributing to the process.
El Niño operates on a much larger canvas, altering atmospheric circulation, wind patterns, moisture availability and the distribution of tropical convection across ocean basins.
Its influence on cyclone formation is not uniformly favourable.

stories.headline: Four earthquakes strike Jammu and Kashmir in 12 hours
stories.title: Four earthquakes strike Jammu and Kashmir in 12 hours
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 14: Four earthquakes of varying magnitudes struck Jammu and Kashmir over a period of around 11 hours on Saturday, with three of the tremors recorded in Doda district and one in Kishtwar. According to the earthquake data, the first tremor, measuring 3.3 on the Richter scale, was recorded in Kishtwar district at 2:38 am, at a depth of 15 kilometres. Three more earthquakes were subsequently recorded in Doda district. reported Kashmir Weather. The second earthquake, measuring 2.7 magnitude, struck at 8:31 am at a depth of 10 kilometres. Seventeen minutes later, at 8:48 am, another tremor measuring 3.8 magnitude was recorded in the district at a depth of five kilometres. The fourth earthquake, measuring 2.9 magnitude, was recorded at 1:09 pm in Doda district, at a depth of 10 kilometres. The repeated seismic activity was concentrated in the Doda–Kishtwar belt, with the strongest tremor measuring 3.8 magnitude.

stories.headline: Cluster of Block Sports Meet Concludes Successfully in Anantnag, Over 150 Youth Participate
stories.title: Cluster of Block Sports Meet Concludes Successfully in Anantnag, Over 150 Youth Participate
stories.summary: Anantnag, Nov 14: Promoting sportsmanship, physical fitness and a drug-free lifestyle among young people, MY Bharat Anantnag successfully concluded a two-day Cluster of Block Sports Meet at Sports Stadium Bijbehara on November 14, organised as part of the 9th Week of the 100 Weeks Campaign under the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan. The two day sporting event, held on November 13 and 14, 2026, was organised under the inspiring theme “Swasth Yuva Viksit Bharat” by MY Bharat Anantnag, functioning under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India. The initiative aimed at encouraging young people to adopt healthy lifestyles, participate in sports and contribute towards building a healthier, stronger and drug-free society. The event witnessed enthusiastic participation from more than 150 young participants, including MY Bharat Volunteers, Youth Club members and students from various educational institutions across the district. The participants displayed remarkable enthusiasm, sporting talent and team spirit throughout the competitions. A total of six sporting events were organised during the two-day programme, providing participants with an opportunity to showcase their abilities across different sporting disciplines. On the first day, a badminton competition for girls was held, witnessing active participation and competitive performances. The second day featured five sporting events, including Volleyball for Boys, Tug of War for Girls, Shot Put for Boys, a 100-Metre Race for Boys and Skipping Rope for Girls. The competitions created an atmosphere of excitement and healthy competition, with participants displaying determination, discipline and enthusiasm. The programme was organised with the broader objective of strengthening the sports culture at the grassroots level and providing young people with constructive platforms to showcase their abilities. It also highlighted the role of sports in developing confidence, leadership qualities, teamwork and discipline among youth. Addressing the gathering, the importance of engaging young people in positive activities and encouraging them to stay away from substance abuse was highlighted. The initiative also reflected the larger vision of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan, which seeks to mobilise youth towards a healthier, more responsible and progressive society. The occasion was graced by international cricketer Mr. Parvez Rasool, who attended the programme as the Chief Guest. International footballer Mr. Mohammad Salah and Mr. Mohammad Shafi, Manager, Sports Council, attended as Guests of Honour. Their presence added significance to the sporting event, while their encouragement and interaction with the participating youth served as a source of motivation for aspiring sportspersons. The participation of prominent sports personalities also underlined the importance of sports in shaping the future of young people and inspiring them to pursue their goals with dedication. At the conclusion of the competitions, certificates and prizes were distributed among the winners and participants in recognition of their performances, enthusiasm and sporting spirit. The organisers appreciated the participation of the youth and acknowledged their efforts in making the two day event a success. The successful conclusion of the Cluster of Block Sports Meet reaffirmed MY Bharat Anantnag’s commitment to promoting youth engagement through sports, awareness programmes and community based initiatives. Such activities are expected to encourage greater participation in physical activities while providing young people with meaningful opportunities to contribute to society. Through initiatives like these, MY Bharat continues to work towards nurturing a generation of healthy, disciplined and empowered young citizens, in line with the vision of a Nasha Mukt and Viksit Bharat.

stories.headline: Yes Bank moves SC seeking review of order on writing off of Rs 8,415 cr AT-1 bonds
stories.title: Yes Bank moves SC seeking review of order on writing off of Rs 8,415 cr AT-1 bonds
stories.summary: Yes Bank has moved the Supreme Court seeking review of its order that upheld Bombay High Court's direction quashing the bank's administrator decision to write off Additional Tier 1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore in March 2020.The bank has sought review of October 15 order of the top court which dismissed appeals challenging the Bombay High Court's January 20, 2023 judgement, which had quashed the write-off.Additional Tier 1 (AT-1) are perpetual bonds issued by banks to increase their capital base and they are riskier than traditional bonds having higher interest rates. The RBI can ask a bank to cancel them if the bank is in trouble.The top court had said the triumvirate of the RBI, the Yes Bank administrator and the Yes Bank in conducting the entire affair of dealing with the bonds worth more than Rs 8,514 crore was questionable."Putting the investors to such uncalled-for risk could have well been avoided. The purpose of the AT-1 bonds is imperative: it acts as a safety barrier to the Bank from collapsing altogether. That purpose could have been served had the RBI and Yes Bank acted in accordance with the terms of the Master Circular."The RBI was a mere bystander, allowing the CET1 ratio of Yes Bank to drop to an astonishing low of 0.6 per cent while the business of Yes Bank was being carried out in a clandestine manner. It cannot be denied that material irregularities in functioning of Yes Bank were noticed much prior; criminal prosecution has also been initiated against the personnel of Yes Bank. However, to have the investors at the receiving end of the administrative lapses would be highly unfair," the Supreme Court had said.It had said the administrator had no authority to write off the bonds in the absence of a specific provision in the reconstruction scheme.The high court had on January 20, 2023 quashed the decision of the Yes Bank taken on March 14, 2020 to write off the bonds, noting that the administrator did not have the authority to take such a decision.The high court, while quashing the decision of the Yes Bank administrator had, however, said its decision will be in abeyance so the central bank and Yes Bank may appeal against it in the apex court.The high court had in its judgment said the final reconstruction scheme of the Yes Bank issued by the Reserve Bank of India did not engulf within its fold writing down the AT-1 bonds."The final scheme sanctioned by the Central government did not contain the clause or provision for writing down AT-1 bonds," it had said.The high court had further held when the RBI prepared the draft scheme for reconstitution of the bank, it had invited suggestions and objections and it appears the petitioners had raised objection to the writing down of AT-1 bonds and even suggested their conversion into shares.The high court had, however, stayed its order for a period of six weeks.The petitions before the high court had also sought directions against National Securities Depositories Limited and Central Depository Services to take steps to reverse the effect of any accounting, entries, noting, write-offs, cancellations, or any such steps that may have been undertaken pursuant to the impugned decision to write off the bonds.After the financial position of Yes Bank underwent a steep decline, on March 5, 2020, the Centre imposed a moratorium on it under section 45 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 till April, 3 2020.On March 14, 2020, the administrator wrote down the AT-1 Bonds which was also communicated to the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange.This act of writing down of the AT-1 Bonds by the administrator was challenged in several writ petitions before the high court. While allowing the challenge, the high court set aside the administrator's action.

opening: Yes Bank has moved the Supreme Court seeking review of its order that upheld Bombay High Court's direction quashing the bank's administrator decision to write off Additional Tier 1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore in March 2020.
The bank has sought review of October 15 order of the top court which dismissed appeals challenging the Bombay High Court's January 20, 2023 judgement, which had quashed the write-off.
body: Additional Tier 1 (AT-1) are perpetual bonds issued by banks to increase their capital base and they are riskier than traditional bonds having higher interest rates.
The RBI can ask a bank to cancel them if the bank is in trouble.

The top court had said the triumvirate of the RBI, the Yes Bank administrator and the Yes Bank in conducting the entire affair of dealing with the bonds worth more than Rs 8,514 crore was questionable." Putting the investors to such uncalled-for risk could have well been avoided.
The purpose of the AT-1 bonds is imperative: it acts as a safety barrier to the Bank from collapsing altogether.

That purpose could have been served had the RBI and Yes Bank acted in accordance with the terms of the Master Circular." The RBI was a mere bystander, allowing the CET1 ratio of Yes Bank to drop to an astonishing low of 0.6 per cent while the business of Yes Bank was being carried out in a clandestine manner.
It cannot be denied that material irregularities in functioning of Yes Bank were noticed much prior; criminal prosecution has also been initiated against the personnel of Yes Bank.
However, to have the investors at the receiving end of the administrative lapses would be highly unfair," the Supreme Court had said.
It had said the administrator had no authority to write off the bonds in the absence of a specific provision in the reconstruction scheme.

The high court had on January 20, 2023 quashed the decision of the Yes Bank taken on March 14, 2020 to write off the bonds, noting that the administrator did not have the authority to take such a decision.
The high court, while quashing the decision of the Yes Bank administrator had, however, said its decision will be in abeyance so the central bank and Yes Bank may appeal against it in the apex court.

The high court had in its judgment said the final reconstruction scheme of the Yes Bank issued by the Reserve Bank of India did not engulf within its fold writing down the AT-1 bonds." The final scheme sanctioned by the Central government did not contain the clause or provision for writing down AT-1 bonds," it had said.

The high court had further held when the RBI prepared the draft scheme for reconstitution of the bank, it had invited suggestions and objections and it appears the petitioners had raised objection to the writing down of AT-1 bonds and even suggested their conversion into shares.
The high court had, however, stayed its order for a period of six weeks.

The petitions before the high court had also sought directions against National Securities Depositories Limited and Central Depository Services to take steps to reverse the effect of any accounting, entries, noting, write-offs, cancellations, or any such steps that may have been undertaken pursuant to the impugned decision to write off the bonds.
After the financial position of Yes Bank underwent a steep decline, on March 5, 2020, the Centre imposed a moratorium on it under section 45 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 till April, 3 2020.
On March 14, 2020, the administrator wrote down the AT-1 Bonds which was also communicated to the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange.
This act of writing down of the AT-1 Bonds by the administrator was challenged in several writ petitions before the high court.
While allowing the challenge, the high court set aside the administrator's action.

sentences.text: Yes Bank has moved the Supreme Court seeking review of its order that upheld Bombay High Court's direction quashing the bank's administrator decision to write off Additional Tier 1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore in March 2020.
The bank has sought review of October 15 order of the top court which dismissed appeals challenging the Bombay High Court's January 20, 2023 judgement, which had quashed the write-off.

The high court had on January 20, 2023 quashed the decision of the Yes Bank taken on March 14, 2020 to write off the bonds, noting that the administrator did not have the authority to take such a decision.
After the financial position of Yes Bank underwent a steep decline, on March 5, 2020, the Centre imposed a moratorium on it under section 45 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 till April, 3 2020.

sentences.text: The bulletin stated, "Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, an elected Member of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), representing the State of Uttar Pradesh, resigned his seat in the Rajya Sabha and his resignation has been accepted by the Chairman, Rajya Sabha w.e.f. 14th November, 2026."
According to a bulletin issued by the Rajya Sabha, Puri's resignation has been accepted by the chairman with effect from November 14.
